doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Accepting musicians and playing the gig you are on
summary: What aggravates him, playing with all kinds of musicians, and his positive Thought of the Day.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I would think there has to be something that might happen on a bandstand or in a recording studio that would aggravate you. And can you think what it might be? Some kind of behavior, either musically or otherwise, from other musicians that you found —

Yeah when they don’t pay me. Oh my God. I get hysterical, are you serious? No, no. No, no. I mean not really. Because I pretty much accept everybody for what they do and what their capability — I played from the greatest, greatest, greatest people on the planet, to the worst that you could ever imagine. And just because somebody is not a great musician doesn’t mean that I don’t — because as I told you earlier man, I’m into people. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

I’ve met with some monster musicians who I wouldn’t go across the street to hang out and have a drink of water with. There’s some guys, I’ve played with a bass player, and he’s a lawyer, and I’ve worked with him for years and years and years. I never heard him play a right note in his life you know. But I actually like going to work with him. And much of my work over the years was going to work, somebody would call me for a gig and I’ll play with some people that I’ve never seen before. And so you make — what do you make out of this? In other words it’s a matter, okay, they call you, what’s the best that you can make out of this situation? And nobody taught me that or anything, that’s just the way it’s always been. You play the gig that you’re on, not the gig that you were on last week or the gig that you hope to be on next week. You play the gig that you’re on tonight. So that’s pretty much it.

Thumbs up for that. I love the, on your website you had a series of “Thoughts of the Day.” And you seem to be an optimist, because on May 4 of 2020 when things were really bad with Covid, and “isolation is the perfect environment to practice” you said. Preparing for the best outcome — “prepare for the best outcome, the worst outcome will take care of itself.”

Yeah I mean that’s not rocket science man. Worst always — you know if a tornado hits — you know you try to get out of its way but you don’t hope for a tornado. So that’s just simple, simple, simple, simple logic man. In other words it’s good and bad — two extremes to everything man. Everything that exists exists in ying and yang you know, man/woman, day/night, you know, winter/summer, whatever. Everything — and there’s a whole lot in between good and evil. And so good force and evil force, I mean they both exist. And so it’s a matter of choice, which do you want to gravitate towards?
